headline: Settlement of 35 Thorpe Avenue tax appeal approved; resolution urges restoring 17 high school classrooms.
summary: Residents spoke during public comment on school crosswalk signs, police conduct, and funding for the Golden Fox Theater. The council also approved naming a softball field at Pragemann Park for Stanley Sheperdsen, who led the Parks and Recreation Department for 28 years.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items 3A through 3D, 3F and 3G. Item 3E was removed.
Approved naming softball field one at Pragemann Park after Stanley Sheperdsen, unanimously.
Approved 8-1 waiving agenda Rule 5 to add discussion of the Pragemann Park storage facility.
Approved 7-2 a resolution asking the Board of Education to restore 17 classrooms to the high school plan.
Approved settlement of the tax appeal filed by 35 Thorpe Avenue Associates LLC, as discussed in executive session.
discussion: School crosswalk signs: Residents asked for signs at school crossings and questioned whether state law requires them. Police said the signs help visibility but cost money and are not in the police budget.
Golden Fox Theater funding: Residents and members debated why a $5,000 allocation had not been paid. The administration said a budget meeting its guidelines is still needed.
Pragemann Park trust: Members questioned whether naming a field could affect about $20,000 a year in trust funds. They cited a 2001 legal opinion on the park's bequest.
Pragemann storage facility: Residents and members debated converting the park pavilion into a storage building for two youth leagues. The project is paid for from the Pragemann Endowment Fund.
High school classrooms: Members debated the 17 classrooms, the changed board votes, and the mayor's memo. They also discussed whether the council should weigh in.
